newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: AIB ups interest rates by up to 0.50 pct.
newsitem.headline: AIB ups interest rates by up to 0.50 pct.

text.p: Allied Irish Banks said it was raising variable interest rates by between 0.25 and 0.50 percent from the close of business on August 27 in response to recent increases in wholesale interest rates.
It said all special savings and notice deposit account rates were being increased by 0.50 percent
-- Its standard variable mortgage rate was being increased on 0.25 percent to 7.35 percent
-- Personal terml loan rates were increased by 0.50 percent
-- Term lending rates to business customers went up by 0.25 percent and business overdraft and loan account rates will rise by 0.45 percent and 0.50 percent respectively
The move followed a similar increase by Bank of Ireland to on Friday.
Ireland's one-month interbank rate has been trading close to 5.75 percent while the official Short Term Facility is at 6.25 percent.
